package_info.why_malicious: No specific malicious package is described in the report. The article discusses the risks and attack strategies associated with leaked credentials and secrets in software supply chains, referencing real-world incidents (CircleCI, Codecov) but not analyzing a particular malware package.

behavioral_signatures: Scanning code repositories for secrets such as API tokens, credentials, and cryptographic keys
Automated validation of discovered tokens to check if they are active
Use of discovered secrets to access cloud services, CI/CD pipelines, or production systems
Alert fatigue due to high volume of secrets scanning alerts
file_indicators: Secrets embedded in source code files (e.g., .env, config.yaml, settings.py)
Secrets in scripts, flat files, or documentation stored in cloud storage (SharePoint, OneDrive, Google Drive)
Secrets in container images or container orchestration files
network_indicators: Unusual access to cloud provider APIs (AWS, Azure, GCP, Slack) using tokens found in repositories
Outbound connections from CI/CD environments to external services using discovered credentials
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Implement automated secrets scanning across all code repositories, CI/CD pipelines, and container images. Use tools that not only detect potential secrets but also validate their activity status to prioritize remediation. Monitor for unusual access patterns to cloud APIs and services, especially from build or deployment environments. Correlate secrets scanning alerts with network activity to identify potential misuse of leaked credentials. Regularly audit storage locations (cloud drives, scripts, documentation) for embedded secrets and enforce least-privilege access controls.
